page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c4g1.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server within the Compute Optimized with GPU instance family, built on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 processor architecture offering 4 dedicated vCPUs paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single integrated NVIDIA P4 graphics processing unit equipped with 8 GB of dedicated VRAM.

The instance does not include local disk storage, requiring network-attached block storage volumes for persistent data retention and operating system deployment. Baseline network throughput is configured at 2 Gbps, and the configuration does not provision complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Because local disk space is absent, all primary I/O operations depend entirely on remote storage volume capabilities and network interface limits.

The hardware profile of ecs.gn5i-c4g1.xlarge is architected for workloads requiring entry-level to mid-range graphics acceleration and machine learning inference rather than heavy distributed model training. With 8 GB of GPU memory and 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs, it is suited for video transcoding, image processing pipelines, deep learning inference tasks, and lightweight parallel computing applications where large local scratch disks are not required.

Operating under the KVM hypervisor within the Compute Optimized with GPU family, this virtual machine maintains a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The server includes no onboard local storage, necessitating remote block storage solutions for operating system installation and application data. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. With its dedicated compute allocation and modest GPU memory envelope, the instance provides cost-efficient acceleration for lightweight visual computing, video encoding, computer vision inference, and medium-scale parallel workloads that do not demand large NVMe local caches or high-tier accelerator architectures.
